content.comment_body: I want to implement a start button that initiates a cycle. When I use [product_name], I set the bit to 1, but it stays active. Can someone assist me?

I have attached an example project consisting of the [product_name] configuration and the related script file. This example demonstrates how to use the web editor to design both a switch and a button. The web server can only send static digital signals, similar to a switch. When you click the button, the web server sets a V-bit to 1, and after the next click, resets it to 0. For push-button behavior, the logic must be handled in the controller program. By using a logic block, you can keep a digital network output at 0 continuously. The network output and its input should share the same address. In the example, this is bit V0.1. When the button is clicked, the web server sets V0.1 to 1. The controller program detects this signal via the network input (V0.1) at state 1, and then the logic block resets the bit through the connected network output (V0.1).
Thank you very much! Nicely done.

Welcome to the forum. If you're using the latest [product_name] version [version_no], this workaround is not necessary. The updated version allows you to choose between a push button or a switch directly in the editor.

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced challenges creating a momentary 'Start' button for cycle control within the web editor, as the default behavior only supports persistent switch-type signals. Feedback indicates that more recent versions of the software now include push-button functionality, simplifying this setup and meeting user requirements.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the web editor to offer a simple push-button option that produces a momentary signal, enabling straightforward cycle initiation.
